title: Quant-iT RiboGreen RNA Quantification Protocol
author: Roey Angel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfbxjipn
materials: Take out all reagents from the fridge and bring them to room temperature. Take out the RNA samples from the freezer. RNA samples should be slowly thawed on ice. Quant-iT™ RiboGreen® RNA reagent is dissolved in dimethylsulfoxide (DMSO), which freezes below 19 °C. The reagent must be completely thawed before using it by bringing it to room temperature. After the reagent thawed, it is advisable to briefly vortex the tube to make sure it is adequately mixed and to spin it down in a centrifuge or a mini centrifuge. Quant-iT™ RiboGreen® RNA reagent is light sensitive and should be protected from light at all times. Quant-iT™ RiboGreen® RNA Assay Kit Thermo Scientific Catalog #R11490

steps.title: Prepare 1X TE Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare 22 ml of 1X TE buffer in a sterile, nuclease-free 50 ml tube.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 1.1 ml of 20X TE buffer into 20.9 ml of nuclease-free water.
Mix by inverting the tube several times.

steps.title: Prepare rRNA-Standard Solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare the rRNA-standard work solutions for high-range and low-range quantification.

substeps.instruction: For high-range: Mix 10 μl of E.coli rRNA-standard stock solution (100 μg ml-1) with 490 μl 1X TE buffer to reach a final concentration of 2 ng μl-1.
For low-range: Mix 10 μl of the 2 ng μl-1 rRNA-standard work solution with 190 μl 1X TE buffer to yield a 0.1 ng μl-1 rRNA-standard work solution.

steps.title: Dilute RNA Samples
steps.instruction: If necessary, dilute each RNA sample in 1X TE so that the reading falls within the dynamic range. It is recommended to run samples in duplicates.

steps.title: Prepare RiboGreen Work Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare the RiboGreen work solution in a sterile, nucleic-acids free 50 ml tube and keep away from light.

substeps.instruction: For high-range assay: Pipette 50 μl Quant-iT RiboGreen RNA Reagent and 9950 µl of 1X TE.
For low-range assay: Pipette 5 μl Quant-iT RiboGreen RNA Reagent and 9995 µl of 1X TE.
Mix by inverting.

steps.title: Set Up 96-Well Plate
steps.instruction: Prepare a black, sterile, flat-bottom 96-well microtiter plate (e.g., Nunc 165305).

substeps.instruction: Prepare standard mixtures in the first two columns.
Pipette 99 µl of 1X TE buffer into the remaining wells.

Pipette 1 µl of the unknown RNA samples into the remaining wells (use diluted samples if concentration is expected to be above the dynamic range limit, or larger volumes if below the detection limit).

steps.title: Add RiboGreen Work Solution
steps.instruction: Pipette 100 µl of the RiboGreen work solution into every well, including standards and unknown samples.

steps.title: Incubate Plate
steps.instruction: Protect the 96-well plate from light and incubate for 2-5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Measure Fluorescence
steps.instruction: Measure fluorescence using a plate reader (e.g., Tecan M Nano) with the following parameters:

substeps.instruction: Excitation: ~480 nm
Emission: ~520 nm
Integration time: 40 s
Lag time: 0 s
Gain: Optimal (or fixed value, e.g., 100)
Number of flashes: 10
Calculated well: highest standard
Shaking: 5 s

steps.title: Calculate RNA Concentration
steps.instruction: Determine the RNA concentration of unknown samples using linear regression.

substeps.instruction: Plot measured fluorescent values of standard samples against known concentrations.
Fit a linear curve (ensure R² > 0.98).
Calculate concentrations in ng µl-1 using the slope and intercept of the linear equation, assuming 1 µl of sample was used.
Account for any sample dilutions in the final calculation.
